s1.syndrome_frame: A chronic, gradually enlarging, itchy skin lesion with ulceration and bleeding on the mid-back
salient_findings: Gradual increase in size over 10 years
Occasional oozing of serosanguineous fluid and bleeding
key_facts: The patient is a woman in her 60s
The lesion has been present since childhood
The lesion was initially asymptomatic and pea-sized
The lesion has gradually increased in size over the past 10 years
The lesion is itchy
There is occasional oozing of serosanguineous fluid and bleeding
The lesion is a well-defined erythematous plaque with overlying ulceration
The lesion is located on the mid-back, 1 cm left of the spine
The adjoining skin shows a horseshoe-shaped oval area of lichenification
Histopathological examination revealed a circumscribed tumor with apocrine epithelial lining
The tumor epithelium has multiple papillary projections with vascular, plasma cell-rich stroma
There are areas of necrosis and atypical cells, but no dermal invasion

Sclerosing sweat duct carcinoma in situ
per_call: Mammary-like gland adenoma of the skin
Sclerosing sweat duct carcinoma in situ

shortlist.label: Hidradenoma papilliferum
shortlist.why_kept: Apocrine gland origin and papillary projections match histopathological findings

shortlist.label: Syringocystadenoma papilliferum
shortlist.why_kept: Papillary projections and apocrine epithelial lining are consistent with the case

shortlist.label: Apocrine hidradenoma
shortlist.why_kept: Circumscribed tumor with apocrine epithelial lining and papillary projections align with the case

shortlist.label: Tubular apocrine adenoma
shortlist.why_kept: Apocrine gland origin and tubulopapillary architecture are plausible given the case facts

shortlist.label: Apocrine gland carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Malignant potential and apocrine gland origin cannot be ruled out given the atypical cells and necrosis

raw.rationale: The presence of a circumscribed tumor with apocrine epithelial lining, multiple papillary projections, and vascular, plasma cell-rich stroma, along with the clinical presentation of a long-standing, gradually enlarging, itchy plaque with ulceration, supports this diagnosis. The histopathological findings, including the absence of dermal invasion, also align with Syringocystadenoma papilliferum.

rejected.label: Hidradenoma papilliferum
rejected.why: Typically presents as a solitary, asymptomatic nodule, which does not match the patient's symptoms of itchiness and oozing.

rejected.label: Apocrine hidradenoma
rejected.why: Usually lacks the papillary projections and vascular, plasma cell-rich stroma seen in this case.

rejected.label: Tubular apocrine adenoma
rejected.why: Not characterized by the complex papillary architecture and ulceration observed in this patient.

rejected.label: Apocrine gland carcinoma
rejected.why: The absence of dermal invasion and the overall architecture of the tumor do not support a malignant diagnosis.
